subject: c10-math
note: For CBSE Class 10 Mathematics Standard (041), 2026-27, the supplied weightage is: Number Systems 6, Algebra 20, Coordinate Geometry 6, Geometry 15, Trigonometry 12, Mensuration 10, Statistics and Probability 11; total theory 80 marks, internal assessment 20. Preparation should emphasize conceptual understanding, problem-solving, visualisation, mathematical communication and applications.

reference.label: Quadratic roots
reference.text: For ax² + bx + c = 0: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a). Discriminant D = b² − 4ac; D>0 gives two distinct real roots, D=0 equal real roots, D<0 no real roots.

reference.label: Pair of linear equations
reference.text: Unique solution: a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂. No solution: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂. Infinitely many solutions: all three ratios equal.

reference.label: Arithmetic progression
reference.text: aₙ = a + (n−1)d and Sₙ = n/2[2a + (n−1)d] = n/2(a+l).

reference.label: Trigonometric standard values
reference.text: Memorise the 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90° values of sin, cos and tan; derive reciprocal ratios when needed instead of memorising unnecessary duplicates.

reference.label: Core identities
reference.text: sin²A + cos²A = 1; 1 + tan²A = sec²A; 1 + cot²A = cosec²A; tan A = sin A/cos A.

reference.label: Heights and distances
reference.text: Draw the right triangle first. Identify the horizontal distance and vertical height, then choose sin/cos/tan. Board-syllabus angles are 30°, 45° and 60°, with no more than two right triangles.

reference.label: Circle sectors and segments
reference.text: Sector area = θ/360° × πr²; arc length = θ/360° × 2πr; segment area = sector area − corresponding triangle area.

reference.label: Surface area and volume
reference.text: Check whether the question asks CSA, TSA or volume. For combinations of solids, calculate only the exposed surfaces required by the diagram.

reference.label: Statistics
reference.text: Grouped-data mean can use direct, assumed-mean or step-deviation method; median and mode use the grouped-data formulas with the correct class interval and cumulative frequency.

reference.label: Probability
reference.text: For equally likely outcomes, P(E) = favourable outcomes / total outcomes; 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1 and P(not E) = 1 − P(E).

reference.label: Real numbers
reference.text: For the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, use prime factorisation systematically; for irrationality questions, know the proof structure for √2, √3 and √5.

reference.label: Polynomials
reference.text: For a quadratic polynomial, connect its zeroes with its coefficients and verify the required relationship algebraically.

reference.label: Triangles
reference.text: For similarity, distinguish and apply AA, SSS and SAS criteria; know the Basic Proportionality Theorem and its converse, including which results require proof.

reference.label: Circles
reference.text: For tangent problems, use the two prescribed theorems: the tangent at the point of contact is perpendicular to the radius, and tangents from an external point are equal.

mistakes: Do not substitute signs carelessly in coordinate, quadratic and linear-equation formulas; write the values first, then simplify.
For geometry proofs, state the theorem or criterion you are using instead of jumping directly to the conclusion.
In trigonometry, draw and label the triangle before choosing a ratio.
In mensuration, distinguish curved surface area, total surface area and volume and attach the correct units.
In statistics, identify l, h, f, cf, f₀, f₁ and f₂ from the correct classes before substituting.
In probability, check that the outcomes being counted are equally likely before applying the classical formula.
order: Algebra first (20 marks): Polynomials → Pair of Linear Equations → Quadratic Equations → Arithmetic Progressions.
Then Geometry (15 marks): Triangles → Circles, with theorem statements and proof practice.
Then Trigonometry (12 marks): ratios → standard values → identities → heights and distances.
Then Statistics and Probability (11 marks), followed by Mensuration (10 marks).
Finish with Number Systems and Coordinate Geometry, while revisiting them through mixed questions.
